plans.quote: There is no monthly plan and no per-seat fee.

plans.name: Custom
plans.quote: Bigger machines, volume pricing, or boxd on your own hardware. For companies of any size.

plans.name: Self-hosted
plans.quote: Self-host it: a single Rust binary you run in your own VPC, datacenter, or country. No Kubernetes, no external Postgres, no Redis. EU data residency, SSO + audit logs, annual license, dedicated support.

planNotes.claim: Every account is an organization with one credit balance; the included machine quota is stated as 100 on the pricing page and the pricing FAQ.

planNotes.quote: There is no monthly plan and no per-seat fee.

compute.cpuBasisNote: vCPU is billed on the machine's full size while it runs, whatever the utilisation. RAM is billed on resident memory, disk on bytes written.
compute.cpuBasisQuote: vCPU is the one component billed on the machine's size: its full vCPU count while it runs, nothing in standby, hibernated or stopped.
compute.ramBasisQuote: RAM bills on the memory a machine actually has resident, sampled every second, while it is running or in standby, not on the 8 GiB it was provisioned with.
compute.diskBasisQuote: Disk bills on the disk you have written to, in every state, not on the 100 GiB provisioned: a machine that has written 20 GiB pays for 20 GiB.
compute.rounding: each of the three meters rounded up to the next millionth of the currency, per settlement window
compute.billingIncrementQuote: Usage is metered every second and settled every 15 minutes: each settlement adds up your organization's vCPU, RAM and disk for that window and charges each of the three rounded up to the next millionth of your currency
compute.minimumQuote: There is no minimum charge per machine, and a partly used window bills only the seconds used.
compute.ratesPerPlan: one rate card for every account; only the currency list (USD or EUR) differs

storage.model: per-GiB-hour on bytes written, in every state
storage.diskIncluded: none; 100 GiB is provisioned per machine but only written bytes are billed
storage.billedWhileStoppedNote: Disk is billed in every state, including hibernated and stopped; vCPU and RAM are not.
storage.quote: Disk bills on the disk you have written to, in every state, not on the 100 GiB provisioned: a machine that has written 20 GiB pays for 20 GiB.
storage.stoppedRetentionNote: No expiry published; a stopped machine keeps its disk until you delete it.

snapshots.note: not published: named snapshots, checkpoints and object-storage backups have no price line on the rate card, and no page states one.
snapshots.quote: Credit-based. You buy credits and your organization's machines draw them down at the rate card: $0.047 per vCPU-hour, $0.014 per GiB-hour of RAM, and $0.000096 per GiB-hour of disk.

hibernation.claim: A hibernated machine bills disk only; a machine in standby also pays for RAM.
hibernation.quote: | **hibernated** (auto-hibernate) | Written to disk | About 85ms | Disk written |

egress.note: The rate card has three meters only (vCPU, RAM, disk). The egress documentation covers allowlisting, not billing. Do not treat it as free.
egress.quote: Credit-based. You buy credits and your organization's machines draw them down at the rate card: $0.047 per vCPU-hour, $0.014 per GiB-hour of RAM, and $0.000096 per GiB-hour of disk.

hermes.summary: boxd has no Hermes-specific page and does not preinstall Hermes. Its 'Personal assistants' page describes the general pattern (create a machine, connect, install the assistant as its own docs say) and names OpenClaw as the example.
steps: boxd new mybot (CLI) or create it in the console
Install Hermes with its installer, then hermes setup and hermes gateway
boxd machine config set mybot auto-hibernate.timeout 0 so the gateway is not hibernated after 4 h without traffic
boxd machine config set mybot bot-protection off if a chat app must reach the machine's public URL
Give it API keys through boxd env / secrets rather than a file on disk

openclaw.route: manual, but named in the docs
openclaw.summary: boxd's Personal assistants page is written around OpenClaw: create a machine, connect, install it, turn off bot protection so chat apps can reach the gateway, and turn off auto-hibernate to keep it always on. It is a documented pattern, not a template or one-click install.

quotes.quote: Run OpenClaw or any other assistant that needs a machine of its own.
Chat apps can't pass [bot protection](https://docs.boxd.sh/guides/bot-protection.md), so turn it off for that machine:

dashboardOnly.answer: Partly. Once a machine exists, the console can open its Desktop, manage Domains and Backups, and start or stop it; the sign-in page offers a prompt to hand to an AI agent that will drive the CLI for you. But every documented first step is a CLI command, and there is no template gallery or one-click agent, so a non-coder cannot provision and install Hermes from the dashboard alone.
dashboardOnly.quote: On the Machines page, open a machine's **Open** menu and choose **Desktop**.

supportingQuote.quote: Install the CLI and create your first machine.
